definition: Cross-lingual Natural Language Inference — the benchmark extending MNLI to 15 languages for evaluating cross-lingual transfer.
details: Cross-lingual Natural Language Inference — the benchmark extending MNLI to 15 languages for evaluating cross-lingual transfer.

explainer.lead: XNLI is a benchmark for testing whether a model trained on English can judge entailment in 15 languages. It matters because it gives a standard, comparable measure of cross-lingual transfer.

tiers.eli5: It is a fixed quiz in fifteen languages, so you can see whether a model taught in one language still answers correctly in the others.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train on English MNLI data and test on translated XNLI to compare transfer strategies such as multilingual pretraining or translation. A common pitfall is using the machine-translated test sets as if they were native text, which can inflate or distort scores.
tiers.paperLevel: XNLI extends MNLI to 15 languages, with premise-hypothesis pairs labelled entailment, neutral or contradiction; results are reported as accuracy averaged across languages, and translation artifacts limit how closely it reflects native-language ability.

explainer.example: A model trained on English MNLI is evaluated on XNLI's translated test sets and its per-language accuracy is averaged to give a single transfer score.
